articles.headline: Man City appeal guilty verdict in Premier League breaches case
articles.description: Manchester City officially lodged an appeal against their guilty verdict in the Premier League financial breaches case.
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・C、プレミアリーグ違反問題の有罪判決に対し控訴
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティは、プレミアリーグの財務違反問題における有罪判決に対し、正式に不服申し立てを行いました。
articles.body:
Manchester City officially lodged an appeal against their guilty verdict in the Premier League financial breaches case.

A statement issued by the club Friday read: "Manchester City Football Club can confirm that at 7pm on Thursday 1st October 2026 the Club lodged its comprehensive Appeal against the opinion of the Premier League Commission, in relation to the Premier League disciplinary matter.

"The Club's firm position is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe.

"The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.

"We will continue to respect due process and are necessarily restricted in what we can say further until all proceedings are complete."

On Tuesday, the Premier League confirmed that City had been found guilty on all of the 100-plus charges of serious breaches of the league's financial rules.

An independent panel concluded that City had artificially inflated the club's commercial revenue by £830 million ($1.1 billion) between 2009 and 2018 through the use of "sham" arrangements. 

- How Man City players, staff are handling Premier League verdict

- Manchester City guilty charges explained: Premier League's options, how appeal works, more

- Downing Street clarifies Andy Burnham's remarks on Man City case

Earlier Friday, the FA expressed concern that City's guilty verdict stains the "integrity" of the game. 

"The Independent Commission's decision has significant implications for the integrity of the game. We are carefully considering the decision and its implications and will take action where appropriate," the FA's statement read.

"As proceedings between the Premier League and Manchester City Football Club remain ongoing, we do not intend to comment further at this stage. We will, however, continue to monitor developments closely."

articles.headlineJa: FA：マンチェスター・シティ裁定は「競技の公平性に重大な影響を及ぼす」
articles.descriptionJa: イングランドサッカー協会（FA）は、プレミアリーグの財務ルール違反を巡るマンチェスター・シティへの有罪判定が競技の「公平性」を損なうとして懸念を表明しました。
articles.body:
The Football Association expressed its concern that the guilty charge aimed at Manchester City over the Premier League's financial rules stains the "integrity" of the game.

The FA's full statement read: "The Independent Commission's decision has significant implications for the integrity of the game. We are carefully considering the decision and its implications and will take action where appropriate.

"As proceedings between the Premier League and Manchester City Football Club remain ongoing, we do not intend to comment further at this stage. We will, however, continue to monitor developments closely."

Friday is the deadline for City to appeal the guilty verdict into their breaches of Premier League rules. They have stated that they intend to appeal.

The commission concluded more than £830 million ($1.1 bn) of such funding was used to inflate revenues and enable the club to comply with Premier League and UEFA financial rules through a series of "sham" arrangements.

The 40-page core decision published Tuesday shows the independent commission rejected the CPC explanation as "untrue" in its findings, adding: "We concluded that it was an 'explanation' that the club had concocted well after the event in an attempt to obscure and conceal the realities of the disguised funding scheme."

Sponsor Etihad Airways, which is owned by an Abu Dhabi fund chaired by City owner Sheikh Mansour's brother, is considering legal action against the Premier League.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham told the BBC earlier this week that he would be concerned if City's owners sold the club due to the guilty verdict because they have been "a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester." But a No. 10 Downing Street spokesman afterwards: "As the Prime Minister made clear, the initial judgement is serious and there can't be any suggestion that anyone is above the rules.

"He also stressed that it is an ongoing independent process. It is essential that it is allowed to run its course and the outcome respected.

"If wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences."

- Manchester City guilty charges explained: Premier League's options, how appeal works, more

- How Man City players, staff are handling Premier League verdict

- Klopp not preparing for more titles after verdict against Man City

But Jamie Carragher wrote for The Telegraph: "The club can only heal and recover from the shame of their guilt once the custodians recognise they have failed in their duty and sell up."

Gary Neville insisted the entire league has suffered due to City's guilty verdict, saying on the Stick To Football podcast on Disney+: "To listen to this, it is chilling.

"We always think that we've got an enormous integrity, the Premier League, that we are the sort of league that sets the standard, and that it's other leagues that have got corruption, fraud, doping scandals, match-fixing, referee scandals.

articles.headline: Where NBA expansion stands ahead of the 2026-27 season
articles.description: As NBA training camps begin for 30 teams, here's the latest intel on the potential for the 31st and 32nd teams.
articles.headlineJa: 2026-27シーズンに向けたNBAチーム拡張の現状
articles.descriptionJa: 全30チームのNBAトレーニングキャンプが始まる中、31番目と32番目のチーム誕生の可能性に関する最新情報をお届けします。
articles.body:
NBA commissioner Adam Silver's news conference in December 2020 was remarkable for several reasons. Similar to many large gatherings during the depth of the COVID-19 pandemic, it was conducted entirely on Zoom. But it was also when he was first asked whether the NBA would consider expansion again for the first time in two decades.

The question, from then-ESPN reporter Tim Bontemps, was framed as a discussion of how the league might recover some of the revenue lost during the pandemic. Silver responded that expansion wasn't on "the front burner," but added that it was "sort of the manifest destiny of the league."

In other words, expansion was inevitable. The only question was when.

First, the NBA focused on securing its new 11-year, $76 billion broadcast deal. Then, it turned its attention to expansion. That process is now nearing its conclusion, with ESPN's Shams Charania reporting this week that the league is expected to select the winning bid for ownership of the Las Vegas team in the very near future, from among three finalist groups.

Here's our latest intel from sources around the NBA on how the final stages of this six-year process could play out.

Where does expansion stand heading into the 2026-27 NBA season?

Silver said he wants a vote on expansion before the end of this calendar year.

That's a broad enough statement to leave a lot of room for negotiations. As it stands, the NBA and strategic adviser PJT Partners, which is handling the process, are more focused on getting a team in Las Vegas, where the interest and bidding have been far more robust than in Seattle.

The expectation is the Las Vegas franchise will go for around $10 billion, with the winning group also expected to spend an additional $2-3 billion to construct a new arena.

As Silver mentioned, there is still discussion among current owners and the bid groups about the best place for a new arena.

A vote on the three groups bidding on Las Vegas -- Nancy Walton Laurie and Bill Laurie; Steve Apostolopoulos and Marc Lasry; and Bill Foley and Jerry Colangelo -- could come soon, sources told Charania.

The runner-up groups could then pivot to Seattle, where Kraken owner Samantha Holloway's group appears to be in pole position, with a valuation sources with knowledge of the process currently estimate to be around $6 billion.

Holloway has tremendous leverage because her company, One Roof Sports & Entertainment, has a majority share of Climate Pledge Arena, which already hosts the WNBA's Seattle Storm and the Kraken and could easily convert to host NBA games as well.

Any other bidder would either have to build their own arena or negotiate with Holloway to use Climate Pledge Arena, a state-of-the-art arena built in 2021, which has also hosted NCAA tournament games. articles.body:
Join the chat as ESPN fantasy football expert Eric Moody will be here to answer all of your start/sit questions and other fantasy-related queries, live from noon to 1 p.m. ET every Friday of the NFL's regular season. 

What's the latest injury buzz as kickoff time approaches? Which player is the better bet for your flex spot? Should you be considering a trade to upgrade your roster? Ask away! Our expert will try to answer as many questions as he can to get you ready for this week's action. 

More advice: Week 4 Rankings | Clay's Playbook | Cockcroft's matchup rankings

Why is my question not getting answered?

Once submitted, your question does not automatically get posted in the chat. Our moderators select which questions they wish to answer and are trying to avoid repeat questions or topics. Scroll back to see if perhaps your question (or one very similar) was answered earlier in the chat.

We are receiving thousands of questions during our hourlong Q&A session and try to get to as many as we can. However, while we appreciate every submission, there is no way we can get to every question that comes in.

articles.body:
The NFL returns to London this week when the Washington Commanders and Indianapolis Colts square off at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The Commanders and Colts are middle of the pack in terms of offensive scoring, but being "mid" is a welcome relief in Tottenham, a club that didn't score their first goals of the English Premier League season until Week 4 against Liverpool. And it didn't score at home until the following week before the international break.

As we head into October, Tottenham is also still winless ... wait a minute, this is supposed to be a fantasy football column.

I will say this about Commanders QB Marcus Mariota, he finds a way to make Terry McLaurin more efficient. McLaurin has notched nine targets in back-to-back weeks, and he has a great matchup against the Colts, who have struggled against the pass this season. And isn't this what Sauce Gardner was supposed to prevent? McLaurin is a great WR2 start this week. On the other side, Josh Downs should have a good opportunity against the Commanders who have given up a league-leading six touchdown receptions to the position this season.

I know it's tough to get up early for these games (though U.S. fans of the EPL are veterans at this), but you're going to want to see this show. And if you're a Tottenham supporter, you're going to want to see people actually scoring in your stadium. Let's look at some other notes you need to know heading into Week 4.

Quarterback notes

What are we doing with our Los Angeles Chargers? Sorry, don't mean "our" like a team we support. But "our" as in players we (mistakenly) drafted. Justin Herbert might still be a start for you because most of the good quarterbacks have already been streamed off waiver. Herbert has yet to top 250 passing yards in a game this season. He has gone four consecutive games with one or no touchdowns dating back to last season. I've made the decision to move on from Herbert and will start Mariota this week, which will probably mean that Herbert will have the week of his life against the Seattle Seahawks in what will be Mike Macdonald's first time facing his former head coach at Michigan. I just can't stand the thought of playing Herbert again.

C.J. Stroud was another streaming option, considering the matchup against the Dallas Cowboys who just recently traded for Joey Porter Jr. The Cowboys have given up more than 27 points per game this season (25th). They have allowed a third-down conversion rate of 59%, which is the worst in the NFL. The matchup is there for Stroud, but there is just something about the Houston Texans' offense that doesn't sit right with me. The return of Nico Collins would help, but I'd rather stick with Mariota or Sam Darnold in desperate times.

articles.headline: Don't be surprised if ... these three hot starters continue to shine all season
articles.description: Don't be surprised if a few early stars stay hot, and if a slow-starting QB enjoys a big Week 4.
articles.headlineJa: 好調なスタートを切ったこの3選手がシーズンを通して活躍し続けても不思議ではない
articles.descriptionJa: 開幕直後に活躍した数名のスター選手が絶好調を維持したり、出遅れたQBが第4週に大活躍を収めても不思議ではありません。
articles.body:
Each week in the NFL is its own story -- full of surprises, both positive and negative -- and fantasy football managers must decide what to believe and what not to believe moving forward. Perhaps we can help. If any of these thoughts come true ... don't be surprised! 

NOTE: All mention of fantasy points is for PPR formats, unless otherwise mentioned.

Don't be surprised if ... New Orleans Saints QB Tyler Shough leads the NFL in passing yards

It is early, yes, but Shough enters Week 4 ranked first in the NFL in pass attempts and second in passing yards, behind only the Panthers' Bryce Young. Young has shown improvement so far, a formidable foe for accruing passing numbers, and we cannot forget about the Rams' Matthew Stafford, Lions' Jared Goff and Cowboys' Dak Prescott, last season's top three in passing yards. The Broncos' Bo Nix threw 612 passes!

Last season, the Saints averaged 93.4 rushing yards per game, 28th in the league. This season, the Saints are faring a tad better, at 101.3 yards per game. But it may be a mirage. Offseason acquisition Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) leads the team, but he will miss at least this Monday's game with the Atlanta Falcons and perhaps multiple weeks. Pass-catching Alvin Kamara is next up, but the Saints may feature Kendre Miller on early downs and save Kamara, 31, for reception work. Shough, sturdy at 6-foot-5, 220 pounds, is a factor with his legs, too, especially at the goal line, but also earning designed runs.

Shough is throwing a ton, on pace for 516 completions on 748 attempts and 5,196 passing yards, along with 45 touchdown passes. Those would be historic numbers. Tom Brady holds the record for pass completions and attempts (490 for 733 with the 2022 Buccaneers), while Peyton Manning set the standard in passing yards (5,477 for the 2013 Broncos). Don't expect Shough to get quite there, but offensive-minded head coach Kellen Moore clearly trusts him, and this team appears attracted to shootouts. We like shootouts in fantasy!

Shough boasts one of the league's top wide receivers in Chris Olave, who is tied for the NFL lead in receptions and second in receiving yards, while Devaughn Vele seems relevant. TE Juwan Johnson ranks third in points at his position (and No. 2 TE Noah Fant has scored three TDs). Dynamic rookie Jordyn Tyson (hamstring), the No. 8 selection in the draft from Arizona State, may return from injured reserve as soon as Week 5. It is easy to see how this passing game thrives all season, for volume and efficiency, even throwing downfield, especially with a friendly schedule.

ESPN Fantasy ranks Shough favorably, for Week 4 and beyond, for good reason. Shough, who was a borderline QB1 option during his nine starts as a rookie last season, is neither young nor inexperienced. This isn't J.J. McCarthy trying to develop, you know. articles.headline: Ranking the top 10 Premier League summer transfers so far
articles.description: Which players have impressed since making a move over the summer? Sometimes a £17 million arrival does better than a £117 million one.
articles.headlineJa: ここまでのプレミアリーグ夏の新加入選手トップ10ランキング
articles.descriptionJa: 今夏の移籍以降、強い印象を残しているのはどの選手でしょうか？時には1700万ポンドで獲得した選手が、1億1700万ポンドの選手を上回る活躍を見せることもあります。
articles.body:
We're just five Premier League games, plus a handful of cup bouts across several competitions, into this fledgling 2026-27 campaign. It's too early to hand down definitive verdicts on the slew of players who moved over the course of yet another big-spending summer, but we can take an early look at which players have settled in quickly and impressed the most at their new clubs.

Here's a top 10, ranked on their overall impact and excellence, taking into account every game they've played so far this term, regardless of competition.

10. Ronald Araújo, RB/CB, Liverpool

Key stat: Liverpool are yet to concede in the league with Araújo on the pitch.

Liverpool have won four of their past five games in all competitions, a jump in form that roughly coincides with Araújo entering the XI. He felt like an opportunistic loan signing from Barcelona (with a €55 million permanent option for next summer) that could go one of two distinct ways, but so far he has been an overwhelming positive.

He has the physique and athleticism to survive the rough-and-tumble of the Premier League, while he's also aware enough of his technical limitations to keep his time on the ball simple, accurate and therefore effective -- except for that sumptuous backheel assist for Dominik Szoboszlai's goal against Atlético Madrid, of course.

9. Christos Tzolis, FW, Arsenal

Key stat: He leads Arsenal in assists in all competitions (four).

Tzolis has brought something different to Arsenal's attack. OK, he wasn't the big-name addition (like Vinícius Júnior or Morgan Rogers) the club craved over the summer, but he has been effective from the start.

His debut in the Community Shield brought two assists, and in general the Greece international winger has added a greater connectivity to the left side as he cuts inside onto his right foot. It hasn't all been positive -- he was poor against Brighton & Hove Albion and taken off at halftime against Aston Villa -- but he has comfortably outperformed his €40 million transfer fee so far.

8. Zion Suzuki, GK, Aston Villa

Key stat: He leads the Premier League in goalkeeper sweeps (7).

Emiliano Martínez's exit from Aston Villa to Chelsea caused plenty of concern among the fans, as he is the club's greatest-ever goalkeeper, but from the moment his replacement Suzuki took to the pitch, those concerns were allayed.

The Japan international possesses a fine combination of smart reflexes and a strong physique, allowing him to fling himself across goal to stop shots and claim crosses among the crowd. His eagerness to race out of his box and sweep up has also stood out among his peers.

But the real story with Suzuki is his incredible distribution. He's not only comfortable with the ball at his feet, he's capable of firing off inch-perfect long passes with both feet to spark counterattacks. The early signs are that Villa have replaced Martínez extremely well.

articles.headline: 2026 NFL trade deadline early look: Candidates to move, key teams, predictions
articles.description: Could the Cardinals listen on Marvin Harrison Jr. or Josh Sweat? Will the Bears or Raiders be active? Here's our way-too-early preview of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
articles.headlineJa: 2026年NFLトレード期限の早期展望：移籍候補選手、注目のチーム、予想
articles.descriptionJa: カージナルスはマービン・ハリソン・ジュニアやジョシュ・スウェットに関する交渉に応じるでしょうか？ベアーズやレイダースは活発に動くでしょうか？11月10日のトレード期限に向けた、超早期プレビューをお届けします。
articles.body:
The NFL's trade deadline is about five and a half weeks away. On one hand, that makes it a little bit early to be talking about who could get moved and where they could go. But on the other hand ... there were already two trades this week! If the Vikings, Giants, Steelers and Cowboys don't think it's too early to talk trades, then neither do we.

So, here's our annual trade deadline lookahead, complete with a list of 10 names who could be on the move for various reasons, five teams we think could be active in trade discussions and a few predictions thrown in at the end just for fun.

Remember: The trade deadline is Nov. 10 (4 p.m. ET), which falls right after Week 9 as the league hits midseason. We don't know for sure which teams will be adding and which teams will be subtracting. A lot of what you'll read below comes with the appropriate disclaimers. If the Raiders keep winning, for example, it's more likely they add than subtract. If the Chargers keep losing, they're more likely to subtract than add. And so on. Nothing here is firm -- we are simply using conversations with team executives around the league to highlight some situations in which roster needs, team fit or contract situations might lead to activity. Let's begin with players to keep an eye on.

Jump to:

10 players who could get traded

Five teams that could be adding

Five predictions for what will happen

10 players who could get traded before the Nov. 10 deadline

Marvin Harrison Jr., WR, Arizona Cardinals

Harrison, the fourth pick of the 2024 draft, is tied for fifth on his own team in targets behind tight end Trey McBride, wide receivers Michael Wilson and Kendrick Bourne and rookie running back Jordan Love. He has the same number of targets (nine) as Tyler Allgeier, the team's No. 2 running back. Harrison has caught four passes for 73 yards in three games (after posting a 41-608-4 line in 2025).

The perception of Harrison from people around the league is that he isn't a fit in an Arizona offense that prioritizes McBride as its top target, and that has led some teams to think he might be available. For their part, the Cardinals have given no indication that they are eager or even interested in trading Harrison. But if he's still an afterthought in the offense a month from now, there are plenty of teams that would be interested in taking a shot on his talent and making him a bigger part of their offense.

Khalil Mack, Edge, Los Angeles Chargers

The Chargers being 0-3 is one of the big surprises of the early part of the season. They expected to be high-level contenders and therefore are not of the mindset to be moving players. If they turn it around and look like the team we expected, then no, I don't think they'd trade their beloved veteran edge rusher.

articles.headline: Kyler Murray's future with Vikings: Clock's already ticking
articles.description: Murray is on a one-year deal with a no-tag clause, so every game counts as both sides assess their future.
articles.headlineJa: カイラー・マレーのバイキングスでの未来：残された時間はすでに動き始めている
articles.descriptionJa: マレーはタグ禁止条項付きの1年契約を結んでおり、双方にとって将来を見極めるための毎試合が重要となる。
articles.body:
EAGAN, Minn. -- The Minnesota Vikings traded quarterback J.J. McCarthy on Monday, 886 days after they made him the No. 10 pick of the 2024 draft. He had played in only 10 games and thrown a total of 243 passes, a snippet in time that coach Kevin O'Connell found himself lamenting afterward. 

The Vikings had tried to identify what McCarthy's "truth and highest potential" was, O'Connell said, "within the timeline that's presented -- not the one that you necessarily would choose going into the whole thing."

To paraphrase baseball great Yogi Berra, it can get late early in the NFL when it comes time to make quarterback decisions. Circumstances don't always grant a generous window of time. It didn't exist for McCarthy, who joined a playoff-ready team when the Vikings drafted him, and it's not present for his successor, either. 

Kyler Murray is playing on a one-year contract with a no-franchise tag clause, meaning both he and the Vikings likely will have to render judgment on his long-term future over the next six months. They are already through 18% of the season, during which Murray has played one full game and 11 snaps of another, and the admittedly small sample size has provided no immediate evidence that he is a sure fit for the team. 

As the Vikings have started 3-0, Murray has completed 52.9% of his passes for 186 yards with one touchdown, two interceptions and four scrambles for 21 yards. Of the 38 quarterbacks who have started at least one game this season, his QBR (17.0) ranks No. 37. 

Both Murray and the Vikings have noted all of the obvious explanations -- Sunday's 23-16 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers was his first full game since October 2025, the Buccaneers' defense ranks No. 6 in EPA, he has played only three series with receiver Justin Jefferson -- while dismissing some of the subjective ones.

General manager Nolan Teasley noted this week, ahead of Sunday's game versus the Miami Dolphins (4:05 p.m. ET, Fox), the "potential" Murray has to succeed with the Vikings and said: "Still looking forward to that coming to fruition, and took some steps forward in that regard [in Tampa]."

Teasley added: "I'm excited about his trajectory in this offense."

The Vikings haven't had a quarterback who plays with Murray's multiplicity of skills in a long time, and it's clear that coaches and players are trying to adjust in real time. Right tackle Brian O'Neill noted there is "no more internal clock" for offensive linemen when they're pass blocking, given Murray's ability to move in the pocket and extend plays. It's a different style than the pocket passers the Vikings have employed in recent years, from Kirk Cousins to Sam Darnold, who were more likely to throw in the scheduled rhythm of a play.

"That's something we're going to have to get with," O'Neill said.
